title: Transactions and Interactive Transactions
description: Master sequential transactions and interactive transactions in Prisma with ACID guarantees, timeout controls, and rollback handling.

data.text: In database systems, a transaction guarantees ACID compliance (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability). If any step within a transaction fails, all preceding mutations are rolled back automatically, preventing corrupt or orphaned records. Prisma provides two transaction patterns: **Sequential Batched Transactions** and **Interactive Transactions**.

When you have independent database operations that do not depend on the return values of previous operations, pass an array of promises to `prisma.$transaction()`. Prisma executes them all within a single `BEGIN ... COMMIT` block in one network roundtrip.

data.title: Sequential Transaction Array
data.content: Deleting an account and resetting counters atomically.

data.text: When an operation requires conditional application logic based on the result of a previous query (e.g. checking a bank balance or verifying ticket inventory before deducting), use interactive transactions. Inside the callback, use the provided transaction client `tx`.

data.title: Financial Transfer with Interactive Transaction
data.content: Guarantees that sender has sufficient balance before transferring money.

data.title: Always Use the `tx` Instance
data.text: Inside the `$transaction(async (tx) => { ... })` callback, you MUST invoke operations on `tx`, NOT `prisma`! Queries called on `prisma` will execute outside the transaction boundary and won't be rolled back if an error occurs.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use array-based `$transaction([...])` for concurrent independent mutations.
Use interactive `$transaction(async (tx) => { ... })` when steps depend on previous results.
Always perform operations using `tx` inside the callback.
Configure `maxWait` and `timeout` to prevent blocking database connections during heavy traffic.
